governing_table.table: Table 403.1, Minimum Number of Required Plumbing Fixtures (Chapter 4 adopted with no changes)
governing_table.quote: The Building Code Standards Committee hereby adopts and incorporates as the Rhode Island Plumbing Code the provisions of the International Plumbing Code (IPC), 2021 edition ... Chapter 4: Fixtures, Faucets and Fixture Fittings. Chapter 4 is adopted with no changes. | Building code (510-RICR-00-00-1): Chapter 29 Plumbing Systems. Chapter 29 is deleted and not adopted as part of the Rhode Island Building Code.
governing_table.note: The adoption and the 'no changes' statement were read on the Department of State's official rules site. The building code's own Table 2902.1 does not apply in Rhode Island because Chapter 29 is deleted.

office.row_label: No. 2, Business: Buildings for the transaction of business, professional services, other services involving merchandise, office buildings, banks, ambulatory care, light industrial and similar uses
office.wc_male: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50
office.wc_female: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50
office.urinals: See Section 424.2 (may replace up to 50% of required water closets)
office.quote: Business | Buildings for the transaction of business, professional services, other services involving merchandise, office buildings, banks, ambulatory care, light industrial and similar uses | WATER CLOSETS: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50 | LAVATORIES: 1 per 40 for the first 80 and 1 per 80 for the remainder exceeding 80 | DRINKING FOUNTAIN: 1 per 100 | 1 service sink

Note d: The occupant load for seasonal outdoor seating and entertainment areas shall be included when determining the minimum number of facilities required.

sex_split.text: The occupant load is divided in half, unless approved statistical data show another split. A shared all-gender room is counted on the whole occupant load instead.
sex_split.quote: 403.1.1 Fixture Calculations. To determine the occupant load of each sex, the total occupant load shall be divided in half. ... Exceptions: The total occupant load shall not be required to be divided in half where approved statistical data indicate a distribution of the sexes of other than 50 percent of each sex. Where multiple-user facilities are designed to serve all genders, the minimum fixture count shall be calculated 100 percent, based on total occupant load.

rounding.text: Fractions round up to the next whole fixture. In a building with several occupancies, the fractions are added first and then rounded up.
rounding.quote: Fractional numbers resulting from applying the fixture ratios of Table 403.1 shall be rounded up to the next whole number. For calculations involving multiple occupancies, such fractional numbers for each occupancy shall first be summed and then rounded up to the next whole number. | Table note a: The fixtures shown are based on one fixture being the minimum required for the number of persons indicated or any fraction of the number of persons indicated.

urinal_substitution.text: Urinals are optional. In each toilet room they may replace no more than 67% of the required toilets in assembly (restaurants) and educational occupancies and no more than 50% elsewhere (offices). The section does not say how the percentage rounds; it is a ceiling, so the worked examples round down. Each urinal needs a privacy screen at least 30 in between partitions, starting no higher than 12 in and reaching at least 60 in above the floor.
urinal_substitution.quote: 424.2 Substitution for Water Closets. In each bathroom or toilet room, urinals shall not be substituted for more than 67 percent of the required water closets in assembly and educational occupancies. Urinals shall not be substituted for more than 50 percent of the required water closets in all other occupancies. | 405.3.5 Urinal Partitions. Each urinal utilized by the public or employees shall occupy a separate area with walls or partitions to provide privacy. The horizontal dimension between walls or partitions at each urinal shall be not less than 30 inches (762 mm). The walls or partitions shall begin at a height not greater than 12 inches (305 mm) from and extend not less than 60 inches (1524 mm) above the finished floor surface.

small_occupancy_exception.text: Separate men's and women's rooms are not required where the total occupant load, staff and customers together, is 15 or fewer; in a business occupancy with 25 or fewer; or in a shop (mercantile) with 100 or fewer. They are also not required where single-user rooms are provided, or where a room is designed for both sexes with each toilet in a compartment.
small_occupancy_exception.quote: 403.2 Separate Facilities. Where plumbing fixtures are required, separate facilities shall be provided for each sex. Exceptions: ... Separate facilities shall not be required in structures or tenant spaces with a total occupant load, including both employees and customers, of 15 or fewer. Separate facilities shall not be required in mercantile occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 100 or fewer. Separate facilities shall not be required in business occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 25 or fewer.

occupant_load.text: The number of occupants comes from the building code's occupant load table: business areas 150 gross sq ft per person, assembly without fixed seats, unconcentrated (tables and chairs) 15 net sq ft per person, classroom area 20 net sq ft per person. Rhode Island adopts that chapter unchanged. Seasonal outdoor seating counts for restaurants.
occupant_load.quote: IPC 403.1: The number of occupants shall be determined by the International Building Code. | IBC Table 1004.5: Unconcentrated (tables and chairs) 15 net | Business areas 150 gross | Educational, Classroom area 20 net. | 510-RICR-00-00-1: Chapter 10: Means of Egress. Chapter 10 is adopted with no changes.

compartments.text: Every toilet used by the public or employees needs its own compartment with walls or partitions and a door, except in a single-occupant room with a lockable door; a child day care room with two or more toilets may leave one without a compartment.
compartments.quote: 405.3.4 Water Closet Compartment. Each water closet utilized by the public or employees shall occupy a separate compartment with walls or partitions and a door enclosing the fixtures to ensure privacy. Exceptions: Water closet compartments shall not be required in a single-occupant toilet room with a lockable door. Toilet rooms located in child day care facilities and containing two or more water closets shall be permitted to have one water closet without an enclosing compartment.

worked_examples.how: 25 women, 25 men. 1 per 25 for the first 50: 25/25 = 1 each. Urinals may replace no more than 50% of 1 toilet = 0.5, so 0.
50 women, 50 men. 1 per 25 for the first 50: 50/25 = 2 each. Urinals: no more than 50% of 2 = 1.
100 women, 100 men. First 50 at 1 per 25 = 2, remaining 50 at 1 per 50 = 1; 3 each. Urinals: no more than 50% of 3 = 1.5, so 1.
200 women, 200 men. First 50 at 1 per 25 = 2, remaining 150 at 1 per 50 = 3; 5 each. Urinals: no more than 50% of 5 = 2.5, so 2.
25 women, 25 men. 1 per 75: 25/75 = 0.33, rounds up to 1 each. Urinals: no more than 67% of 1 = 0.67, so 0.
50 women, 50 men. 50/75 = 0.67, rounds up to 1 each. Urinals: 0.
100 women, 100 men. 100/75 = 1.33, rounds up to 2 each. Urinals: no more than 67% of 2 = 1.34, so 1.
200 women, 200 men. 200/75 = 2.67, rounds up to 3 each. Urinals: no more than 67% of 3 = 2.01, so 2.
25 girls, 25 boys. 1 per 50: 25/50 = 0.5, rounds up to 1 each. Urinals: no more than 67% of 1, so 0.
100 girls, 100 boys. 100/50 = 2 each. Urinals: no more than 67% of 2 = 1.34, so 1.
200 girls, 200 boys. 200/50 = 4 each. Urinals: no more than 67% of 4 = 2.68, so 2.

hdpe_fire.section: Rhode Island Building Code RISBC-1 (2021 IBC), Section 803.9, with 803.1.1 and 803.1.1.1 (NFPA 286 room-corner test). Chapter 8 and Chapter 2 are adopted with no changes; the Chapter 2 definition of interior wall and ceiling finish names toilet room privacy partitions.
hdpe_fire.quote: 803.9 High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE) and Polypropylene (PP). Where high-density polyethylene or polypropylene is used as an interior finish, it shall comply with Section 803.1.1. | 803.1.1 Interior Wall and Ceiling Finish Materials Tested in Accordance With NFPA 286. Interior wall and ceiling finish materials shall be classified in accordance with NFPA 286 and comply with Section 803.1.1.1. | [BF] Interior Wall and Ceiling Finish: The exposed interior surfaces of buildings, including but not limited to: fixed or movable walls and partitions; toilet room privacy partitions; ... | 510-RICR-00-00-1: Chapter 8: Interior Finishes. Chapter 8 is adopted with no changes.
hdpe_fire.note: 'Adopted with no changes' read on the official rules site; the section text read on UpCodes' copy of the Rhode Island Building Code 2021. The Rhode Island Fire Safety Code (450-RICR-00-00-1 to 10) was not read; it may carry its own interior finish rule.

access.state_standard: Chapter 11 of the 2021 International Building Code, adopted in the Rhode Island Building Code with no changes, which requires compliance with ICC A117.1. The edition listed in Chapter 35 of the 2021 IBC is ICC A117.1-2017 (Rhode Island's only change to Chapter 35 is a general statement). There is no separate state-written access code. The federal 2010 ADA Standards apply alongside, so a stall has to meet the stricter of the two on each point. State law directs the code committee to keep its rules consistent with the ADA (R.I. Gen. Laws 23-27.3-100.1.5(d)).

differences.state: The side wall needs a vertical grab bar, at least 18 in long, in addition to the horizontal bar. It applies in the wheelchair stall and on both sides of the ambulatory stall.
differences.federal: Side wall: one horizontal bar, 42 in minimum (604.5.1). No vertical bar.
differences.quote: 604.5.1 Fixed Side-Wall Grab Bars. Fixed side-wall grab bars shall include a horizontal bar complying with Section 604.5.1.1 and a vertical grab bar complying with Section 604.5.1.2. ... 604.5.1.2 Vertical Grab Bar. A vertical grab bar 18 inches (455 mm) minimum in length shall be mounted with the bottom of the bar located 39 inches (990 mm) minimum and 41 inches (1040 mm) maximum above the floor, and with the center line of the bar located 39 inches (990 mm) minimum and 41 inches (1040 mm) maximum from the rear wall. | Federal 604.5.1: The side wall grab bar shall be 42 inches (1065 mm) long minimum, located 12 inches (305 mm) maximum from the rear wall and extending 54 inches (1370 mm) minimum from the rear wall.

differences.state: 12 in high and 8 in deep under the front partition and one side partition of the wheelchair stall. Not needed at the front where the stall is deeper than 64 in (wall-hung toilet) or 67 in (floor-mounted), or at the side where it is wider than 68 in.
differences.federal: 9 in high and 6 in deep; not needed at the front where the stall is deeper than 62 in (wall-hung) or 65 in (floor-mounted), or at the side where wider than 66 in (604.8.1.4).
differences.quote: 604.9.5.1 ... The front partition and at least one side partition of wheelchair accessible toilet compartments shall provide a toe clearance of 12 inches (305 mm) minimum above the floor and extending 8 inches (205 mm) beyond the compartment side face of the partition, exclusive of partition support members. Exceptions: Toe clearance at the front partition is not required in a wheelchair accessible toilet compartment greater than 64 inches (1625 mm) in depth with a wall-hung water closet, or greater than 67 inches (1700 mm) in depth with a floor-mounted water closet. Toe clearance at the side partition is not required in a wheelchair accessible toilet compartment greater than 68 inches (1725 mm) in width. | Federal 604.8.1.4: The front partition and at least one side partition shall provide a toe clearance of 9 inches (230 mm) minimum above the finish floor and 6 inches (150 mm) deep minimum beyond the compartment-side face of the partition ...

differences.point: How many accessible stalls in a large restroom
differences.state: At least 5% of the compartments in a room must be wheelchair accessible, and where toilets and urinals together total six or more, at least 5% must be ambulatory accessible in addition. Above 20 compartments this means more than one of each.
differences.federal: At least one wheelchair accessible compartment, plus at least one ambulatory compartment where there are six or more compartments or six or more toilets and urinals combined (213.3.1).
differences.quote: 1110.2.4 Water Closet Compartment. Where water closet compartments are provided in a toilet room or bathing room, at least 5 percent of the total number of compartments shall be wheelchair accessible. Where the combined total water closet compartments and urinals provided in a toilet room or bathing room is six or more, at least 5 percent of the total number of compartments shall be ambulatory accessible, provided in addition to the wheelchair-accessible compartment. | Federal 213.3.1: Where toilet compartments are provided, at least one toilet compartment shall comply with 604.8.1. In addition ... at least one compartment shall comply with 604.8.2 where six or more toilet compartments are provided, or where the combination of urinals and water closets totals six or more fixtures.

differences.state: Outlet 24 to 36 in from the rear wall if above the grab bar, 24 to 42 in if below, and 18 to 48 in above the floor. The federal position (7 to 9 in in front of the toilet) is allowed only for a dispenser holding at most two rolls of 5 in diameter. A small dispenser placed 7 to 9 in in front of the toilet meets both.
differences.federal: Centerline 7 to 9 in in front of the toilet; outlet 15 to 48 in above the floor; not behind grab bars (604.7).
differences.quote: 604.7.1 Location. Where the dispenser is located above the grab bar, the outlet of the dispenser shall be located within an area 24 inches (610 mm) minimum and 36 inches (915 mm) maximum from the rear wall. Where the dispenser is located below the grab bar, the outlet of the dispenser shall be located within an area 24 inches (610 mm) minimum and 42 inches (1065 mm) maximum from the rear wall. The outlet of the dispenser shall be located 18 inches (455 mm) minimum and 48 inches (1220 mm) maximum above the floor. Exception: Toilet paper dispensers that accommodate a maximum of 2 toilet paper rolls of not more than 5-inch (125 mm) diameter each shall be permitted to be located 7 inches (180 mm) minimum and 9 inches (230 mm) maximum in front of the water closet ... | Federal 604.7: Toilet paper dispensers shall comply with 309.4 and shall be 7 inches (180 mm) minimum and 9 inches (230 mm) maximum in front of the water closet measured to the centerline of the dispenser.

differences.state: Restaurants and other assembly buildings, and shops, need an accessible single-user family or assisted-use room where six or more toilets are required in total. Its door must lock from inside and show an 'occupied' indicator.
differences.federal: No requirement to provide a unisex room; 213.2.1 only sets what one may contain and requires a privacy latch.
differences.quote: 1110.2.1 Family or Assisted-Use Toilet and Bathing Rooms. In assembly and mercantile occupancies, an accessible family or assisted-use toilet room shall be provided where an aggregate of six or more male and female water closets is required. ... 1110.2.1.6 Privacy. Doors to family or assisted-use toilet and bathing rooms shall be securable from within the room and be provided with an "occupied" indicator. | Federal 213.2.1: Unisex toilet rooms shall contain not more than one lavatory, and two water closets without urinals or one water closet and one urinal. ... Doors to unisex toilet rooms and unisex bathing rooms shall have privacy latches.

differences.point: Wheelchair turning space in the room (new buildings)
differences.state: 67 in diameter circle in new buildings, 60 in in existing buildings. It must be in the room and cannot be inside a stall. This sets the room layout around the stalls, not the stall itself.
differences.federal: 60 in diameter (304.3.1; not re-read for this pack).
differences.quote: 304.3.1.1 New Buildings and Facilities. In new buildings and facilities, the turning space shall be a circular space with a 67-inch (1700 mm) minimum diameter. ... 304.3.1.2 Existing Buildings and Facilities. In existing buildings and facilities, the turning space shall be a circular space with a 60-inch (1525 mm) minimum diameter. | 603.2.1 Turning Space. A turning space shall be provided within the room. The required turning space shall not be provided within a toilet compartment.

differences.state: Looser than the federal rule: the door opening in the front partition may be either within 4 in of the side farthest from the toilet or at least 56 in from the side closest to it. The federal 4 in rule still applies, so it governs.
differences.federal: Door opening 4 in maximum from the side wall or partition farthest from the toilet (604.8.1.2).
differences.quote: TABLE 604.9.3.1 DOOR OPENING LOCATION: Front Wall or Partition | From the side wall or partition closest to the water closet | 56 inches (1420 mm) minimum | or | From the side wall or partition farthest from the water closet | 4 inches (100 mm) maximum | Federal 604.8.1.2: Where located in the front partition, the door opening shall be 4 inches (100 mm) maximum from the side wall or partition farthest from the water closet.

access.same_as_federal: Read and found the same in both: wheelchair stall 60 in wide and 56 in deep (wall-hung) or 59 in (floor-mounted); ambulatory stall 35 to 37 in wide and 60 in deep; self-closing door with a pull on both sides; rear grab bar 36 in minimum; children's wheelchair stall 59 in deep with 12 in toe clearance.
access.process: No state plan-review or project-registration step for accessibility was found. Accessibility is part of the state building code, which the local building official enforces through the building permit. State law tells the Building Code Standards Committee to keep its rules consistent with the ADA (R.I. Gen. Laws 23-27.3-100.1.5(d): 'The state building code standards committee is hereby authorized and directed to update those rules and regulations consistent with the future revisions of the Americans with Disabilities Act Accessibility Standards.'). Search results (not opened) say the School Building Authority has local school departments send design plans to the Governor's Commission on Disabilities for review; confirm before using.

single_user.rule: State law: every single-user toilet facility in a public building or place of public accommodation must be available to persons of any gender. A sign is optional, but if used it must mark the room as a restroom and not indicate one specific gender. New state and municipal buildings open to the public, and renovations of them above 50% of value, must provide a single-user room. The plumbing code says the same about identification and counts these rooms toward the required total.
single_user.quote: R.I. Gen. Laws 23-27.3-702(a): Notwithstanding any other provision of the general or public laws to the contrary, any single-user toilet facility in a public building or place of public accommodation that exists or is constructed on or after January 1, 2023, shall be made available for use by persons of any gender, and designated for use by not more than one occupant at a time or for family or assisted use. A single-user toilet facility may be identified by a sign; provided, that the sign marks the facility as a restroom and does not indicate one specific gender. (b) All new construction of state and municipal buildings opened to the public commenced after July 1, 2021, and all renovations and replacements of a value in excess of fifty percent (50%) of existing public state and municipal buildings open to the public commenced after January 1, 2022, shall provide for a single-user toilet facility available for use by persons of any gender. | IPC 403.1.2: Single-user toilet and bathing rooms, and family or assisted-use toilet rooms and bathing rooms shall be identified as being available for use by all persons regardless of their sex.

all_gender_shared.rule: Allowed by the plumbing code. Separate rooms for each sex are not required where a room is designed for both sexes and every toilet is in its own compartment with walls or partitions and a door; urinals must be in a visually separate area or each in a stall. The fixture count for such a room is worked out on the whole occupant load. The code does not require floor-to-ceiling partitions.
all_gender_shared.quote: 403.2 exception: Separate facilities shall not be required where rooms having both water closets and lavatory fixtures are designed for use by both sexes and privacy for water closets is provided in accordance with Section 405.3.4. Urinals shall be located in an area visually separated from the remainder of the facility or each urinal that is provided shall be located in a stall. | 403.1.1 exception: Where multiple-user facilities are designed to serve all genders, the minimum fixture count shall be calculated 100 percent, based on total occupant load. In such multiple-user facilities, each fixture type shall be in accordance with ICC A117.1 and each urinal that is provided shall be located in a stall.

use_restrictions.rule: No Rhode Island law restricting restroom use by sex in particular buildings was found. The public accommodations law bars denying facilities on account of sex or gender identity or expression, and a separate section says the law's references to sex do not mandate joint use of restrooms by males and females.
use_restrictions.quote: R.I. Gen. Laws 11-24-2: No person, being the owner, lessee, proprietor, manager, superintendent, agent, or employee of any place of public accommodation, resort, or amusement shall directly or indirectly refuse, withhold from, or deny to any person on account of race or color, religion, country of ancestral origin, disability, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, any of the accommodations, advantages, facilities, or privileges of that public place. | 11-24-3.1: Nothing contained in this chapter that refers to "sex" shall be construed to mandate joint use of restrooms, bath houses, and dressing rooms by males and females.

restrooms.confidence_note: Statutes read on the legislature's site (high). Plumbing code sections on UpCodes (medium). 'No restriction found' rests on the statutes read, not on an exhaustive search.

public_wage.law: R.I. Gen. Laws Chapter 37-13 (Labor and Payment of Debts by Contractors), with 260-RICR-30-15-3, Rules and Regulations Relating to Prevailing Wages. Covers public works of the state, any city or town, and public or quasi-public agencies, including alteration and repair of public buildings.
public_wage.rates_set_by: The Director of Labor and Training, who adopts the federal Davis-Bacon General Wage Decisions; contractors must update to the new rates each July 1.
public_wage.rates_url_note: Not opened: dlt.ri.gov returns HTTP 403 to automated access. The rates themselves are the federal General Wage Decisions for Rhode Island on sam.gov.
public_wage.quote: 37-13-3: All contractors, who have been awarded contracts for public works by an awarding agency or authority of the state or of any city, town, committee, or by any person or persons therein, in which state or municipal funds are used and of which the contract price shall be in excess of one thousand dollars ($1,000) ... and their subcontractors, on those public works shall pay their employees at weekly intervals and shall comply with the provisions set forth in 37-13-4 to 37-13-14 and 37-13-16. | 37-13-8: In making a determination, the director of labor may adopt and use such appropriate and applicable prevailing wage rate determinations as have been made by the secretary of labor of the United States of America in accordance with the Davis-Bacon Act ... | 260-RICR-30-15-3.3(J): "Prevailing wage" means the Base Hourly Rate of Pay plus the Fringe Benefit Credit which are listed on the General Wage Decisions, 40 U.S.C. 3142 (2017), developed by the U.S. Department of Labor and adopted by the Rhode Island Department of Labor and Training ...

sales_tax.rate_quote: R.I. Gen. Laws 44-18-18: ... for the period commencing July 1, 1990, the tax rate is seven percent (7%). | 44-18-20(h): The use tax imposed under this section for the period commencing July 1, 1990, is at the rate of seven percent (7%).
sales_tax.local_rates_note: No city or county sales tax on general goods was seen in the statutes or the Division's contractor guide, whose examples all use 7%. The Division's rate page (tax.ri.gov) could not be opened; the city agent should confirm Providence adds nothing.

shipped_goods.rule: Taxable at 7%. A remote seller with $100,000 or more in gross revenue from Rhode Island sales, or 200 or more transactions, in the previous calendar year must register and collect the tax. Where the seller does not collect it, the buyer is liable for use tax.
shipped_goods.quote: 44-18.2-3(E): ... any remote seller ... [that] in the immediately preceding calendar year either: (i) Has gross revenue from the sale of tangible personal property ... delivered into this state equal to or exceeding one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000); or (ii) Has sold tangible personal property ... for delivery into this state in two hundred (200) or more separate transactions. | (I): A remote seller, referrer, and marketplace facilitator shall register in this state for a permit to make sales at retail and collect and remit sales and use tax on all taxable sales into the state. | 44-18-21(a): Every person storing, using, or consuming in this state tangible personal property ... purchased from a retailer ... is liable for the use tax. The person's liability is not extinguished until the tax has been paid to this state ...

sales_tax.freight_quote: 44-18-12(a): "Sales price" ... means the total amount of consideration ... without any deduction for the following: ... (iv) Delivery charges, as defined in 44-18-7.1(i). | 44-18-7.1(i): "Delivery charges" means charges by the seller of personal property or services for preparation and delivery to a location designated by the purchaser of personal property or services including, but not limited to: transportation, shipping, postage, handling, crating, and packing.

install_labor.rule: Not taxed when the charge for installing the property sold is stated separately on the bill. The retailer must state it separately when the buyer asks. If the installation charge is not separated from the price of the goods, the whole charge is taxed.
install_labor.quote: 44-18-12(b): "Sales price" shall not include: ... (ii) The amount charged for labor or services rendered in installing or applying the property sold when the charge is separately stated by the retailer to the purchaser; provided that in transactions subject to the provisions of this chapter the retailer shall separately state such charge when requested by the purchaser ... | Division of Taxation, Contractors & Rhode Island Tax (February 2024): Installation labor separately stated is not subject to sales tax. ... When the retail selling price of the tangible personal property is not separately stated from the installation charge, the entire charge is subject to sales tax.

furnish_and_install.rule: On a construction contract (repair, alteration, improvement, remodeling or construction of real property), the contractor pays the tax as the consumer of the materials when buying them. Two exceptions make the contractor a retailer who collects tax from the customer on the goods: where the contract sells materials at an agreed price with the service charged separately, and where the contractor sells and installs a complete unit of standard equipment the way a retailer does (the tax then applies to the price of the goods only, if the installation charge is separated). The Division's regulation and guide do not name toilet partitions, so which treatment a partition supply-and-install job gets is open. Contractors on jobs for the state, a Rhode Island city or town, or a nonprofit with an exemption certificate may buy the materials tax-free.
furnish_and_install.quote: 280-RICR-20-70-54.6(A)(1): A contractor shall pay the tax as a consumer on the purchase of all materials, supplies, tools and equipment ... used by him in fulfilling either a lump-sum contract, a cost-plus contract, a time and material contract with an upset or guaranteed price which may not be exceeded, or any other kind of construction contract except: a. where the contractor contracts to sell materials or supplies at an agreed price and to render service in connection therewith, either for an additional agreed price or on the basis of time consumed, or: b. where such contractor is engaged in the business of selling such materials or supplies at retail. | 54.6(C): This regulation is not applicable to contracts whereby the contractor or subcontractor acts as a retailer selling tangible personal property in the same manner as other retailers and is required to install a complete unit of standard equipment, requiring no further fabrication but simply installation, assembling, applying or connecting services. ... A person performing such contracts is primarily a RETAILER ... and should segregate the full retail selling price of such property from the charge for installation, as the tax applies only to the retail price of the property. | 54.5(B): "Construction contract" means a contract for the repair, alteration, improvement, remodeling or construction of real property.

sales_tax.nonresident_contractor_note: Anyone awarding a construction contract in Rhode Island to a contractor with no regular place of business in the state must withhold 3% of the contract price until the Tax Administrator clears the contractor's taxes (280-RICR-20-70-54.8; R.I. Gen. Laws 44-1-6). Relevant to out-of-state installers, not to buying partitions.
sales_tax.confidence_note: Statutes and the regulation read on official sites, plus the Division's own guide (PDF). The Division's web pages (rate page, remote seller page) return HTTP 403 and were not opened.

page.stalls_intro: Rhode Island's rules count toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. Half are counted as men and half as women, and any fraction rounds up. Every toilet needs a stall. Urinals are optional: in each men's room they may replace up to half of the toilets in an office and up to two thirds in a restaurant or school, and each urinal needs a privacy screen. The table shows all the men's fixtures as stalls.
page.stalls_after: These are minimums for the whole building, and the same table applies in every Rhode Island city and town. An office holding 25 people or fewer, or any space holding 15 or fewer, may use one restroom for everyone, and a restaurant's seasonal outdoor seating counts toward its capacity.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, the building rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20.
page.fire_bullet: - **Fire safety:** Rhode Island's building rules require solid plastic (HDPE) and polypropylene partitions to pass a room-corner fire test. Ask for the fire-rated version.
page.access_bullet: - **Wheelchair access:** a restroom with stalls needs at least one stall a wheelchair user can enter and use. Federal law and Rhode Island's building rules both set the sizes, and the local building official checks them with the building permit. No separate state review step was found.
page.state_extra_bullet: - **Rhode Island extras:** the state's rules add to the federal ones in a few places. The accessible stall needs a vertical grab bar, at least 18 inches long, beside the horizontal one on the side wall. Where a partition must leave toe space underneath, it is 12 inches high, against 9 inches federally. In a large restroom, 5% of the stalls must be wheelchair accessible. A restaurant or shop that needs six or more toilets in total must also have a single-user family restroom.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** Rhode Island law makes every one-person restroom in a public building or a business open to the public available to any gender. A sign is optional, and if there is one it must say restroom without naming one gender. A shared all-gender room is allowed if every toilet sits in its own compartment with a door and urinals are in stalls or screened from view.
page.public_jobs: On state, city, town and public school projects over $1,000, Rhode Island law requires at least the prevailing wage, which the state Department of Labor and Training takes from the federal wage decisions and updates each July 1.
page.tax_install_bullet: - **Tax on installation:** in Rhode Island, a charge for installing what you bought is not taxed when it is listed separately on the bill, and the seller must list it separately if you ask. On a construction contract, the contractor pays the tax on the materials when buying them. Ask the Rhode Island Division of Taxation which rule covers a partition supply-and-install job.
page.tax_ship_bullet: - **Buying without installation:** partitions shipped to {city} are taxable at 7%, freight included. If the seller doesn't collect the tax, the buyer owes it to the state.
page.tax_confirm: your accountant or the Rhode Island Division of Taxation

notes: Chapter 29 of the IBC (the building code's own fixture table) is deleted in Rhode Island, so the plumbing code's Table 403.1 is the only fixture table.

R.I. Gen. Laws 23-27.3-702(e) tells the Building Code Standards Committee to adopt rules for the gender inclusive restroom act; no such rule was seen in RISBC-1 or RISBC-3. A municipality may ask the committee for a waiver for undue burden (702(c)).
Rhode Island's Fire Safety Code is separate from the building code (450-RICR-00-00-1 to 10) and was not read.
A117.1-2017 also changes other things outside the stall (for example clear floor space in new buildings); only stall and restroom-layout points that were read are listed.
The existing-building codes (RISBC-7 Existing Building Code, Part 20 Rehabilitation Code) were not read; they decide how much of the above applies to a like-for-like partition replacement.
